title: How President Trump Broke the Kennedy Center
partialText: Internal emails and documents demonstrate the political capture of the institution, including how officials once pursued a plan to unload much of the art collection.

title: Trump Faced Loss After Loss. He Then Turned to a Familiar Target: The Press.
partialText: The president’s ban of three media outlets from the White House fits a pattern of using the apparatus of government to crack down on his perceived enemies.

title: Markwayne Mullin Lost His Pick to Lead ICE, as He Struggles to Prove His Toughness on Immigration
partialText: Markwayne Mullin is working to overcome hard-liners’ doubts about his leadership, his position undermined by missteps with the White House.

title: Trump Says His D.C. Arch Would Be a ‘Military Complex’ Housing Drones and Snipers
partialText: The president’s announcement on Sunday echoed his justification for the White House ballroom: that the project was necessary for national security.

title: Houthis Push to Expand Territory as Tensions With Saudi Arabia Rise
partialText: The Iranian-backed militia was engaged in fierce battles with Saudi-backed government forces in Yemen on Sunday, as it seeks to maintain momentum in the war.

title: In Fighting for Every Black Child, Did I Betray My Own?
partialText: A decade ago, I made a decision about my daughter’s education that I hoped would challenge New York City’s separate and unequal school system. Now 16, she thinks I made the wrong choice.

title: Reality Bites
partialText: We look at how one mother approached the decision of where her child should go to school.

title: In China, A.I. Is Moving Forward While the Economy Lags Behind
partialText: As Xi Jinping arrives in the United States this week for a state visit, China’s advances in artificial intelligence will be in the air. Less discussed: China’s economy in its worst shape in decades.

title: Troy Jackson, a Progressive Brawler, Tries to Flip a Senate Seat in Maine
partialText: Mr. Jackson landed in the race unexpectedly. Democrats are hoping he can unseat Susan Collins, a Republican, in their bid to retake the Senate.

title: Abdul-El Sayed, a Democrat, Has an Unlikely Defender: Tucker Carlson
partialText: Mr. Carlson, the far-right podcaster, has promoted Dr. El-Sayed’s comments and sharply criticized his Republican rival in a key Senate race. Strategists are scratching their heads.

title: Hundreds of Drones Target Moscow on Final Day of Russian Elections
partialText: Ukraine says it used a newly developed ballistic missile in the attacks, which also targeted other parts of Russia.

title: Russia Barred Their Party, but These Antiwar Voices Are Still Standing
partialText: The liberal party Yabloko is fielding 98 candidates in this weekend’s elections, a small miracle for antiwar Russians who cannot openly express their views.

title: A.G. Sulzberger: The Story of America, Told in 15 Million First Drafts of History
partialText: The Times has witnessed the country’s transformation. It will keep its eyes open.

title: Mistakes? We’ve Made a Few
partialText: For most of its life, The New York Times has tried to correct its errors. These efforts have not always been perfect.

title: Is Audrey Hobert the Most Honest Voice in Pop?
partialText: The rising pop star talks songwriting with her BFF Gracie Abrams, knowing when to log off and the difference between being weird (yes!) and awkward (no way).

title: There Is Something We Have to Do Right Now About A.I.
partialText: Letting A.I. patrol its own frontier is like asking Jesse James to patrol the Wild West.

title: The End of American Exceptionalism?
partialText: Liberal democracy is in worldwide retreat, including in its birthplace — the United States.

title: American Yom Kippur: How Jews Across the U.S. Observe the Holiest Day of the Year
partialText: From 200-mile treks to synagogue to spiritual striving, readers share the rituals that define Judaism’s holiest day for them.
